SHAPE+ is driving standardization and automation of core Accounting and Cost Accounting processes as well as Master Data Management for Post & Parcel, DHL Express, DHL eCommerce & Group Functions through rolling out a SAP-based FINANCE template with respective system consolidations. Our vision is to have the most advanced, most efficient and innovative Finance ERP platform established that supports capabilities like continuous accounting as well as real-time data processing & analytics. As Platform Lead PTP/Banking in the SHAPE+ team, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and driving our global SAP S/4HANA Finance platform for Procure-to-Pay (PTP) and Banking processes. Leveraging your expertise in Accounting, Invoice-to-Pay, and SAP S/4HANA Finance, you will deliver scalable, standardized solutions across our global organization combining elements of: * Solution Governance: Own and design solutions fitting to the global PTP/ Banking template, while folding-in local deviations if legally required, in the process of implementing the template across business divisions and geographies* In-depth Process Knowledge: Commitment to harmonizing Accounting and Controlling processes in consultation with process teams and being a trusted advisor for ERP implementation, to other SMEs and business colleagues alike* Platform Advisory: Translate business and process requirements into robust techno-functional solutions, configure the ERP platform, and oversee a stable of expert implementation partners to ensure top-notch quality in an agile project environment* Continuous Improvement: Champion innovation in your area by investigating and identifying opportunities to improve operational efficiency and automation, while ensuring the platform evolves alongside business needs & SAP best practices* Leadership Mindset: Foster a collaborative, performance culture by demonstrating strong analytical and conceptual skills, resilience and an outcome-oriented approach, ensuring the success of the program* Additionally, knowledge in S4/HANA Material Management & MM-Inventory Management or Purchasing would be a plus – but not mandatory. Exposure to SAP BTP and CAS services, integration technologies such as REST/SOAP/oData, SAP Public Cloud projects and emerging SAP AI capabilities such as Joule 2.0 is welcomed A must? University Degree in Business Informatics (or similar), superior English skills (German a plus) and relocating to the Bonn/Cologne area, if necessary.  Who suits us? Curious people who like to deep-dive into new topics, never losing sight of the big pictureLateral thinkers who courageously question the status quo and strategize best fit solutionsPurposeful people who want to make a positive impact to our Group’s successEnthusiasts constantly looking for the best UX, process & IT solutionsPioneers who are not afraid of making the impossible possible Your benefits* Competitive compensation package with 20% variable part* Company pension plans and other forms of retirement provision* Salary conversion for environmentally-friendly commuting, leasing of company bicycle or lease of electric company car. Alternatively conventional vehicles available, too * Flexible working arrangements, such as part-time options or remote work possibilities* Health and well-being initiatives, such as sabbaticals or measures to promote a healthy work-life balance incl. health management initiatives, including preventive check-ups, sports activities* Work-family balance by offering company day care facilities in Bonn and cooperation with pme Familienservice, offering services such as childcare during school holidays* Opportunities for further education and development, such as training / mentoring programs, workshops, or support for professional growth. Fast-paced development opportunities driven by best practices and cutting-edge solutions, keeping up with the latest trends and technologies* Collaborate with executives and senior management in the global finance community, contributing to strategic decision-making processes and become a game changer in the largest Finance transformation in the industry* Emphasis on respect and results and the opportunity to make a positive impact, such as through corporate social responsibility initiatives or involvement in charitable projects, Go Teach, Go Help, Global Volunteer Day, taking part in team-building activities or company event, such as summer party, Bonn Marathon etc.* Subsidized Germany-wide public transportation ticket and various employee discounts and offers from external providers  A highly committed team – diverse, international and fun group of skilled people that has the unique chance to make a massive contribution to our Finance unit, being exposed to positively impacting thousands of colleagues around the globe.  Your ideas & suggestions will greatly come into play. We need people that take accountability to drive things ahead, ramping up required skills along the way, fully visible and supported by senior executives and team members.  Your contactFor further information on the post, Sarah Pinapati, Head of Global Finance Platforms will be happy to answer your questions, therefore please contact sarah.pinapati@dhl.com. The application deadline is three weeks.This is a non-tariff managerial position (AT nicht leitend)  CONNECTING PEOPLE, IMPROVING LIVES

WE ARE LOOKING FOR YOU ASPRODUCT SOFTWARE ENGINEER (BACK END JAVA) (M/W/D)LIMITED IN COLOGNEInterzero is one of the leading service providers in closing product, material, and logistics cycles and a pioneer in plastics recycling, operating Europe’s largest sorting capacity. Guided by the principle of “zero waste solutions,” the company supports more than 80,000 customers across Europe in the responsible handling of recyclable materials, helping them improve their sustainability performance and conserve primary  resources. With around 2,000 employees, Interzero generates annual revenues of nearly one billion euros. According to Fraunhofer UMSICHT, Interzero’s recycling activities alone saved approximately 1.04 million tons of greenhouse gas emissions and 8.09 million tons of primary raw  materials compared to primary production in 2024. Further information at: www.interzero.de.What is it about?- Collaboration: Together with Product, UX and Front-End colleagues, design and implement the Java back ends of both brand-new and evolving products you’ll stay with for the long haul.- Modeling: Translate business goals into sturdy domain models and reliable services that deliver real customer value.- Architecture: We’re moving toward a headless, microservice-oriented landscape. Your ideas are welcome.Advantages:- Job Security: You can expect a varied, exciting, and secure role with one of the largest environmental service providers in a future-proof industry.- Compensation: You receive performance-based pay with a strong focus on maintaining your work-life balance.- Flexibility: You benefit from flexible working hours and the option to work remotely.- Creative Freedom: You work in an environment where ideas, initiative, and creative freedom are encouraged and supported.- Flat Hierarchies: You operate within flat hierarchies and quickly take on responsibility for your own tasks.- Collaboration: You experience a culture of collaboration and respect at eye level, both within and beyond your team.- Development: You have access to internal and external training and development opportunities.- Health: You benefit from a comprehensive health management program.- Benefits: You receive attractive perks such as corporate benefits, bike leasing, free drinks and fruit on-site, and coverage of the Germany ticket or an Edenred card.Profile:- Experience: 5 + years of professional Java experience, ideally with Spring Boot and Hibernate/JPA.- Expertise: Deep knowledge of RESTful API design, relational databases (MySQL/PostgreSQL), and containerization with Docker.- Frontend-Familiarity: Familiarity with our frontend technology stack (React/Next.js/TypeScript) can be advantageous; if you want to work full-stack, you can.- DevOps: Familiarity with GitLab CI/CD — our DevOps team handles the heavy lifting, but you know your way around.- Architectural Judgment: A sense for clean architectures, test automation, and the judgement to choose the right pattern at the right time.- Languages: Fluent English (German is a bonus), a collaborative mindset and genuine curiosity about how products succeed in the real world.- EU-Work: A valid EU work permit; candidates already based in Germany (or nearby EU countries) are strongly preferred.Contact:Yannick Bartschhr@interzero.deErgänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Grundkenntnisse: Softwarearchitektur, Software testenErweiterte Kenntnisse: Datenbankadministration, -management, -organisation, REST (Representational State Transfer), Java Persistence API (JPA), Backend-Entwicklung, Programmiersprache Java

The University Hospital Bonn (UKB) is one of Germany’s leading university hospitals, combining top-level performance in medicine and research with excellence in teaching. Each year, more than half a million patients receive inpatient and outpatient care at the UKB. Around 3,500 students study medicine and dentistry here, and over 600 people are trained annually in healthcare professions. With approximately 9,900 employees, the UKB is the third-largest employer in the Bonn/Rhein-Sieg region. In the Focus hospital ranking, the UKB ranks first among university hospitals in North Rhine-Westphalia and second nationwide in terms of case mix index (case severity). In 2024, the UKB raised nearly €100 million in third-party funding for research, development, and teaching. The F.A.Z. Institute has named the UKB “Germany’s Training Champion” and “Germany’s Most Attractive Employer” for the fourth consecutive year.The following full-/part-time position (38.5/19.5 hours per week)  is to be filled as soon as possible in the Institute for Hygiene and Public Health, Section Global Child Health of the University Hospital Bonn:Scientific coordinator (m/f/d)The Section of Global Child Health was established in November 2025 with the appointment of the Endowed Professorship in Global Child Health. The Section’s remit includes research and teaching in Germany and internationally, as well as clinical practice and the applied, practice-oriented engagement with global health challenges affecting children and adolescents. The professorship is structured as a tandem appointment with a corresponding position at the University of Malawi, based in Lilongwe.You will work in close collaboration with the section head in establishing sound research and communication networks with partners in Malawi and GermanyThe professorship focuses on research in the area of neonatal, child, and adolescent health in “Low and Middle Income Countries” (LMICs), identifies barriers to and solutions for improving global child health, and facilitates the transfer of epidemiological and clinical evidence into health care services with the goal of improving the health status of all children globally.It facilitates institutional, national and international networking and collaboration with universities, academic institutions and key development partners.In addition, it provides academic and health policy advice to national and international governmental as well as non-governmental organizations with regard to global child health.The position is initially limited to three years and remunerated according to TV-L EG 13 (German tax ID is a prerequisite). If you currently live abroad, you should be willing to relocate to Germany temporarily. Subject to interest and feasibility, a temporary increase in the scope of employment through third-party funded resources is envisaged.Tasks:This position offers the opportunity to actively contribute to the development of global strategies for improving children's health and to build and design a completely new international research and education structure.- Strategic coordination and management of international research, education and clinical programmes across the two professorships and the EKFS network- Planning, coordination, and monitoring of cross-institutional activities with academic and non-academic partners- Management of communication channels between institutions, disciplines, and countries, ensuring efficient information flow and alignment of activities- Coordination, and implementation of training materials and structured capacity-building programmes in collaboration with international experts- Planning, organisation, and delivery of international workshops and seminars in online and on-site formats- Preparation of annual progress and impact reports, dissemination of results through conferences and other scientific communication formats- Contribution to the strategic development, coordination, and drafting of third-party funding proposals to expand and sustain programme activitiesRequirements:- A full academic degree at Master’s level or higher in a health-related discipline- A strong interest in global child health and international health systems cooperation- Demonstrated experience in project coordination and research management- Excellent organisational skills and a structured, meticulous approach to work- Proven ability to navigate academic hierarchies and university administrative processes, combined with sensitivity to intercultural contexts- Strong teamwork skills, resilience, and the ability to assert and represent set positions- Full professional proficiency in both German and English, written and spoken Willingness to maintain an appropriate on-site presence at the university in Bonn- Previous extended study, research, or professional experience in a low- or middle-income country would be considered a strong assetWe offer: An interesting and challenging job in a modern research institution with attractive research infrastructures and a cooperative and communicative institute culture. This includes:- **Responsible and diverse: **A position with significant scope for initiative and development within a truly collegial and supportive team- **Fair compensation: **Pay according to the TV-L collective agreement, including annual bonus and company pension scheme- **Family-friendly flexibility: **Flexible working time models, access to a place in our company daycare center, and programs supporting employees returning from parental leave- **Smart commuting: **Excellent connection to the SWB public transport network and the option of an interest-free loan for the purchase of an e-bike- **Supported development: **Individual training opportunities through courses, e-learning programs, and coaching sessions- **Structured onboarding: **A systematic introduction to your new role and team- **Healthy at work: **A wide range of health and wellness programs, plus free membership at the UKB fitness studio- **Employee benefits: **Access to discounted offers for employees (corporate benefits)We are committed to diversity and equal opportunities. Our goal is to increase the proportion of women in areas where women are underrepresented and to particularly promote their careers. We therefore urge relevantly qualified women to apply. Applications are treated in accordance with the State Equal Opportunities Act. Applications from suitable people with proven severe disabilities and those of equal status are particularly welcome.How to apply:If you are seeking a challenging and internationally oriented position within a leading research and clinical environment, we would be pleased to hear from you. For further information, please feel free to contact us.Please submit your complete application documents by 28/02/2026, quoting the vacancy reference number [ST-37032], as a single PDF file (maximum size 5 MB), by email to the address below.English is the working language in many areas of the position; sound knowledge of German is required for administrative issues. Support services for international applicants may be available, including guidance on visa and residence matters as well as initial orientation and integration. Information on dual career options and local infrastructure can be provided upon request.Prof. Dr. med. jobs.occupation: Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**Overview

**The Associate Director, Trial Delivery Team Lead plays a key leadership role in overseeing Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs) while supporting the broader Clinical Trial Management (CTM) organization. This individual ensures high-quality clinical trial execution by providing strategic guidance, mentorship, and operational oversight. The Line Manager is responsible for team development, resource allocation, process optimization, and ensuring alignment with organizational goals and regulatory standards. The Trial Delivery Team Lead may assume Global Trial Lead (GTL) responsibilities to address fluctuating demands.

**Roles & Responsibilities

****Leadership and Line Management:

**

• Directly manage, mentor, and develop Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and Clinical Trial Associates (CTAs), fostering professional growth.

• Conduct performance evaluations, provide feedback, and identify training and career development opportunities.

• Ensure adequate resourcing, workload distribution, and succession planning within the team.

• Facilitate cross-functional collaboration and knowledge-sharing within the clinical operations team.

• Collaborate with Global Trial Leads (GTLs) on trial activities for assigned direct reports.

• Support trial deliverables by facilitating progress, coaching, and mentoring CTMs and CTAs.

• Advise on resource needs and support overall clinical trial resource planning.

• Ensure team success through setting clear expectations, guiding performance, and leading competency development.

• Lead functional working groups; serve as process owner or Subject Matter Expert (SME) within Clinical Operations.

• Support training initiatives across Trial Operations as needed.

• Collaborate with senior leadership to define and implement best practices within the Development Operations organization.

**Process & Compliance Management

**

• Ensure team adherence to Good Clinical Practice (GCP), ICH guidelines, and regulatory requirements (FDA, EMA, etc.).

• Develop and refine Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to optimize trial efficiency and compliance.

• Support audits, inspections, and regulatory interactions by ensuring inspection readiness across clinical trials.

• Identify and drive process improvements to enhance trial execution and data quality.

• Lead cross-trial initiatives as needed, such as implementation of Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs) or new process rollouts across the program.

• Manages the execution and implementation of CTM and CTA tasks, ensuring operational success.

• Initiates and supports the development of processes within the CTM and CTA group, focusing on practical application and continuous improvement.

• Collaborates across functions to drive efficiencies and provide day-to-day guidance to the CTM and CTA groups.

**Requirements – What You Must Have

**

• Bachelor of science degree with relevant specialization; Master of science degree preferred

• Minimum requirement of 12 or more years of experience in clinical operations

• Significant experience in leading and managing complex global clinical projects/programs

• Significant experience managing/guiding internal (cross-functional) and external (CRO, regulatory authorities) teams

• Experience with operational management and budget planning

• Proven performance in earlier role/comparable role

• Global clinical program level experience required

• Experience within the field of oncology is preferred

• Minimum 2 years’ experience as Clinical Operations representative in Clinical Development Teams (CDTs) or Global Project Teams (GPTs) would be preferable

• Experience leading team members in global matrix environment, leveraging tools and technology to ensure business needs are met.

• Strategic thinking with ability to optimize organizational resources for successful program execution

• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken

**Moreover, You Meet The Following Personal Requirements

**

• Dedicated team player who enjoys leading teams and inspire trust among colleagues

• Quality mindset and able to prioritize your work in a fast paced and changing environment

• Result- and goal-oriented and committed to contributing to the overall success of Genmab

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$158,720.00---$238,080.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.

jobs.occupation: Senior Product Manager, Scientific Software — Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Senior Product Manager, Scientific Software — Copenhagen

The company

Our client is a venture-backed Copenhagen biotech that designs a new class of oral drugs. It uses its own generative AI, automated chemistry and high-throughput biology. The platform has made and tested hundreds of thousands of novel compounds, and the company has a major pharma partnership behind it. R&D is organised under a CTO across three groups: AI & Computational Drug Design, Platform Chemistry, and Screening Biology.

The role

The Senior Product Manager will own the company's internal scientific software, so every team works from the same clean, consistent data with tools that fit together.

The company creates, moves and decides on large volumes of chemistry and biology data. Today each team builds its own solutions. The company is moving to a new data platform built for its molecules and will build custom internal products on top of it.

The Product Manager is the person who sees that three teams are building three versions of the same thing and turns them into one that works for everyone. Success is measured in time saved for the scientists: the software should save more than it costs.

Responsibilities

Product ownership

• Owns the roadmap for the internal scientific software, starting with the three products above.

• Gathers and challenges requirements from computational design, chemistry and biology, and turns parallel requests into shared solutions.

• Prioritises with the leadership team: what gets built, in what order, and why.

• Makes sure the products connect to each other and to the data platform.

• Runs user testing and adoption with the scientists, and tracks the time saved.

Delivery and leadership

• Works agile, and knows where agility stops. Ships working products within months without painting the platform into a corner.

• Leads and coordinates 3–6 developers, a mix of contractors and hires. A front-end engineer may report directly.

• Helps shape the software team as it grows.

Hands-on, at the start

• Contributes to the build until the development team is in place. The stack is Python on the back end, React/Redux on the front end, and AWS serverless services.

• Judges which components fit together and which will break, including AI-assisted code.

The profile

The ideal candidate has experience from an environment where software is built and shipped, and a scientific background. Beyond that, in order of importance:

• People leadership. Has led developers or cross-functional teams, internal or contracted, and aligned stakeholders who don't report to them.

• Product management track record. Has owned a software product or platform from idea to adoption.

• Drug discovery experience. Has worked close to design, synthesis, screening or compound selection. Broader R&D software is also relevant.

• Scientific background. A chemistry or biology degree (either is fine). Knows what they don't know, and asks.

• Hands-on coding. Can build in Python and React. Judgement matters more than depth.

Mindset: curious enough to ask "what's a canonical SMILES?", pragmatic about agile, and happy to start hands-on and grow into leading a team.

Nice to have: AWS serverless, lab automation or screening data, ELN/LIMS or compound registration, startup or scale-up experience. The working language is English.

Set-up, package and process

• Reporting. To the VP of AI & Computational Drug Design, with a weekly 1:1 and short daily stand-ups.

• Location. On site in Copenhagen, enough to work alongside the chemists and biologists in the lab. There is no fixed number of days.

• Career path. Starts senior and hands-on, and grows into leading a dedicated software team.

• Package. A competitive salary, pension, a performance bonus, and participation in the company's warrant programme.

• Process. A short screening call, then an online session where the candidate presents software they have built, then on-site interviews. The target start is early 2027.

Join Pharmacosmos in a newly established function, in a role combining people leadership with direct involvement in clinical processes, compliance and continuous improvement.

Build and lead a new Clinical Administration & Compliance function

As Director, Clinical Administration & Compliance, you will report directly to the Senior Director, Head of Clinical Operations, Trine Kolding, and take on a key role combining leadership with hands-on responsibility for clinical trial administration, processes and operational GCP compliance.

You will lead and develop the Clinical Administration and Process Management functions, setting clear priorities and direction while fostering collaboration, accountability and high-quality delivery. At the same time, you will remain actively involved in developing, implementing and continuously improving processes that support effective and compliant clinical trial execution across R&D.

A key responsibility will be to translate ICH-GCP, regulatory expectations and internal requirements into practical, risk-based ways of working. You will contribute directly to operational compliance, documentation practices, TMF quality, sponsor oversight and inspection readiness, ensuring that processes are robust, pragmatic and consistently applied. Working closely with trial teams and stakeholders across R&D, you will identify opportunities to simplify and strengthen processes and drive improvements through implementation.

A hands-on leader who enjoys making compliance work in practice

The ideal candidate brings extensive experience from clinical research or clinical development within the pharmaceutical, biotechnology or CRO environment, combined with strong practical knowledge of ICH-GCP and the processes and documentation required to execute and oversee clinical trials. You have hands-on experience with clinical trial processes, SOP implementation, TMF and essential documentation, as well as inspection readiness.

You have gained leadership experience, ideally within Clinical Operations, Clinical Process Management or a related area, while remaining motivated by direct involvement in the work. Experience working across functions and navigating multiple stakeholders within an R&D and trial-execution environment is essential.

You genuinely enjoy working with clinical processes, compliance and continuous improvement and are motivated by a role that combines leadership with hands-on responsibility. You bring a pragmatic and risk-based mindset, enabling you to translate regulatory requirements into practical ways of working while balancing compliance, simplicity and effective trial delivery.

As a person, you are structured, collaborative and confident in engaging stakeholders across Clinical Operations and the wider R&D organization. You are comfortable setting direction and priorities while staying close to the details, and you have the judgement and drive to identify areas for improvement and turn them into sustainable ways of working. You communicate clearly at all levels and have the natural authority to engage and motivate people. You are fluent in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

Join a highly collaborative Clinical Operations team

You will join a highly collaborative Clinical Operations environment built on trust, ownership and strong collegial relationships. We learn from each other, share responsibility and solve new challenges together rather than working in silos.

As Pharmacosmos continues to grow, you will have a genuine opportunity to shape how we work as the organization develops and make a visible contribution to both Clinical Operations and the wider R&D organization.

Play a crucial role in an exciting international growth journey

This is your chance to embark upon a personal and organizational journey in a dynamic company where your know-how is greatly needed for the future development of Pharmacosmos. The recruitment process is carried out by Venaris Executive Search. For more information regarding the position, please reach out to Sr. Executive Search Consultant, Lars Nordlund, on +45 3123 3018. All requests will be handled confidentially. If this position is for you, do not hesitate to apply by uploading your CV - it is not necessary to include a cover letter.

Pharmacosmos

Pharmacosmos A/S is a global leader in carbohydrate chemistry and innovative treatments for iron deficiency and iron deficiency anaemia. Building on our foundational expertise in carbohydrate chemistry and cell cycle biology, we develop innovative treatments for unmet patient needs, with a focus on iron metabolism and blood-related disorders. Founded in 1965 and headquartered in Denmark, our team is made up of more than 650 specialists across the UK, Ireland, the Nordics, Germany, Canada, and the USA. Learn more about Pharmacosmos at www.pharmacosmos.com.
